text:
Situation: Rifampin injection has been on the FDA shortage list since 2021-02-17 and remains Current as of 2026-10-21. The listing covers Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC (NDC 63323-351-20), Mylan Institutional (NDC 67457-445-60), and Sanofi-Aventis U.S. LLC (NDC 0068-0597-01). Our Corvale sites hold Mylan-labeled 600 mg/10 mL vials (NDC 67457-445-60) manufactured by OneSource Specialty Pharma Limited in Bengaluru. Corvale East has 4.4 days on hand for the 10 mL vial; Corvale Lakeside has 29.5 days; Corvale General has 15.8 days.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the shortage on 2021-02-17 and it remains Current as of 2026-10-21. FDA inspected Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC (FEI 1450022) on 2020-05-18 and classified it OAI, 275 days before the shortage posting. A later Fresenius inspection on 2022-06-30 was also classified OAI, and a 2023-08-24 inspection was classified VAI.

Our position: We have sufficient aggregate stock across sites but an imbalance leaves Corvale East critically low on the 10 mL vial. The Mylan product we hold is on the FDA shortage list. Alternate presentations from Fresenius and Mylan are also listed as Current on the FDA shortage list.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 17 vials of rifampin 600 mg/10 mL, 10 mL vial from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East — needs pharmacy director approval for transfer request.
2. Transfer 7 vials of rifampin 600 mg/10 mL, 10 mL vial from Corvale General to Corvale East — needs pharmacy director approval for transfer request.
3. Evaluate purchase from Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. — not on FDA shortage list today; label names no plant we could place — needs buyer approval.
4. Use alternate concentration or vial size: Rifampin 600 mg/10 mL from Mylan Institutional LLC — recalculate dose and volume; pharmacist verification required; approved by Casey Nguyen, MD on 2026-06-26; FDA lists this product Current (posted 2021-02-17) — needs pharmacist approval.
5. Use alternate concentration or vial size: Rifampin 600 mg/1 from Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC — recalculate dose and volume; pharmacist verification required; approved by Jordan Hale, PharmD on 2026-09-01; FDA lists this product Current (posted 2021-02-17) — needs pharmacist approval.

Not recommended: No clinical dosing changes or therapeutic substitutions; those are for treating clinicians and the committee.
